questions.question: If 60% of a number is added to 120, then the result is the number itself. 60% of this number is _______.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If 60% of a **number** is added to 120 to get the **number itself** (100%), it means the added 120 represents the **remaining 40%**.

⇒ 40% of the number = 120

⇒ 1% of the number = 120 ÷ 40 = 3

⇒ 60% of the number = 3 × 60 = 180

**∴ The correct answer is 180.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 60% of a **number** + 120 = the **number**.

**Formula Used:** Percentage value = (Percentage / 100) × **Total Value**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/63ec03d6f2f68dd03b93461254430e61052955ac6b752015dd3d347c27bac0ac.png] 

⇒ Let the **number** be x.

⇒ 60% of x + 120 = x

⇒ (60 ÷ 100) × x + 120 = x

⇒ 0.6x + 120 = x

⇒ x − 0.6x = 120

⇒ 0.4x = 120

⇒ x = 120 ÷ 0.4

⇒ x = 300

Now, we need to find **60% of this number**:

⇒ 60% of 300 = (60 ÷ 100) × 300

⇒ 0.6 × 300 = 180

**∴ The correct answer is 180.**

**__Additional Information__**

Base Value Concept

In percentage problems, the **original number** is always treated as the **base** (100%). Any addition or subtraction is relative to this base.

Fractional Equivalents

Converting percentages to **fractions** simplifies calculation: 60% = 3/5 and 40% = 2/5. If 2/5 of a number is 120, then 3/5 is (120 ÷ 2) × 3 = 180.

Percentage Change Formula

The percentage increase or decrease is calculated as: (Change ÷ Original Value) × 100.</p

questions.question: If x : y = 8 : 3, then (x + y) : (x - y) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly apply the **Componendo and Dividendo** logic to the given ratio.

If **x : y = 8 : 3**, then **(x + y) : (x − y) = (8 + 3) : (8 − 3)**.

Calculation: **11 : 5**.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The ratio **x : y = 8 : 3**.

**Formula Used:**

For any ratio **x : y = a : b**, we can assume **x = ak** and **y = bk**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e7c3fa4b8a19ed2af319d5540a9a1b29f3ddd7830e85b7052ab0276e40c4ea6e.png] 

Let **x = 8k** and **y = 3k**, where **k** is a constant.

⇒ **x + y = 8k + 3k = 11k**

⇒ **x − y = 8k − 3k = 5k**

⇒ **(x + y) : (x − y) = 11k : 5k**

⇒ **(x + y) : (x − y) = 11 : 5**

**∴ The correct answer is 11 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If **a/b = c/d**, then **(a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d)**. This property is extensively used to simplify ratios involving addition and subtraction.

Invertendo and Alternando

**Invertendo**: If **a : b = c : d**, then **b : a = d : c**. **Alternando**: If **a : b = c : d**, then **a : c = b : d**.

Duplicate and Sub-duplicate Ratio

The **duplicate ratio** of **a : b** is **a² : b²**, and the **sub-duplicate ratio** is **√a : √b**.</p

questions.question: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF with BC : EF = 1 : 4. Find the area(Δ DEF) : area(ΔABC).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two **similar triangles**, the **ratio of their areas** is equal to the **square** of the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.

Given side ratio **BC : EF = 1 : 4**.

⇒ Area(ΔABC) : Area(ΔDEF) = 1² : 4² = 1 : 16.

⇒ Area(ΔDEF) : Area(ΔABC) = **16 : 1**.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **ΔABC ∼ ΔDEF**

⇒ Ratio of sides **BC : EF = 1 : 4**

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔDEF) = (BC ÷ EF)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3199c69e49572c0acd01a9021c529651a018f860f9ba70145a5c1e88ff1b6b2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ According to the **Area Theorem** of **similar triangles**:

⇒ Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔDEF) = (BC)² ÷ (EF)²

⇒ Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔDEF) = (1)² ÷ (4)²

⇒ Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔDEF) = 1 ÷ 16

⇒ Area(ΔABC) : Area(ΔDEF) = 1 : 16

⇒ Inverting the ratio to find **Area(ΔDEF) : Area(ΔABC)**:

⇒ Area(ΔDEF) : Area(ΔABC) = 16 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 16 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Similar Triangles Area Theorem

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of any two corresponding sides, altitudes, or medians.

Perimeter Ratio

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides (linear ratio).

SAS Similarity

Two triangles are similar if two sides of one triangle are proportional to two sides of another triangle and their included angles are equal.</p

questions.question: 48 men can do a work in 5 days while 40 women can do the same work in 9 days. In how many days can 4 men and 6 women together do the same work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Equate work to find **Efficiency** ratio: 48 Men × 5 days = 40 Women × 9 days.

⇒ 240 Men = 360 Women ⇒ 2 Men = 3 Women ⇒ **1 Man : 1 Woman = 3 : 2**.

Convert **4 Men + 6 Women** into **Women** units: 2(3W) + 6W = **12 Women**.

Using **M₁D₁ = M₂D₂**: 40 Women × 9 days = 12 Women × D₂.

⇒ D₂ = 360 ÷ 12 = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **48 men** = 5 days

Time taken by **40 women** = 9 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of persons × Efficiency × Days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Total Individual Days**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency (Unit/Day)**
 
 

 1 Man (48 × 5)
 240 days
 720 units
 3 units
 
 

 1 Woman (40 × 9)
 360 days
 2 units
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **1 Man** = 3 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of **1 Woman** = 2 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of **4 Men** = 4 × 3 = 12 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of **6 Women** = 6 × 2 = 12 units/day

⇒ Total efficiency of **(4 Men + 6 Women)** = 12 + 12 = 24 units/day

⇒ Required Days = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Required Days = 720 ÷ 24 = 30 days

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

MDH Rule

For work comparison, use (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂, where M is persons, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work. Ratio of efficiency A:B = x:y implies ratio of time A:B = y:x.

Combined Work

When multiple groups work together, their total efficiency is the sum of their individual efficiencies (Total E = E₁ + E₂ + ... + Eₙ).</p

questions.question: A person saves 30% of his monthly income. If his monthly income increases by 20%, then he saves 20% more than the previous savings. The percentage increase in his expenditure is ___.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If every component of a sum (**Income = Expenditure + Savings**) increases by the same percentage, the total sum also increases by that same percentage.

Here, the **Income** increases by **20%** and the **Savings** also increases by **20%**.

By the rule of uniform percentage change, the **Expenditure** must also increase by **20%** to maintain the balance.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Savings** = 30% of **Income**

Increase in **Income** = 20%

Increase in **Savings** = 20%

**Formula Used:**

**Income = Expenditure + Savings**

**Percentage Increase = [(New Value − Old Value) / Old Value] × 100**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/906503951f49a15d33e1f6968f7f988563a706ea8a9612882d03bac0170a1111.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let initial **Income** = 100

⇒ Initial **Savings** = 30% of 100 = 30

⇒ Initial **Expenditure** = 100 − 30 = 70

⇒ New **Income** = 100 + (20% of 100) = 120

⇒ New **Savings** = 30 + (20% of 30) = 30 + 6 = 36

⇒ New **Expenditure** = New **Income** − New **Savings**

⇒ New **Expenditure** = 120 − 36 = 84

⇒ Increase in **Expenditure** = 84 − 70 = 14

⇒ Percentage Increase = (14 / 70) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = (1 / 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Income Identity

The total monthly earnings of an individual are always distributed as **Income = Expenditure + Savings**.

Weighted Average Property

If **Income** increases by **x%** and **Savings** increases by **y%**, the percentage change in **Expenditure** is governed by the ratio of initial expenditure and savings.

Constant Proportions

If all parts of a whole increase by the same percentage, the whole and its constituent ratios remain constant relative to each other.</p

questions.question: The LCM of two numbers is 84. If the numbers are in the ratio 2 : 3, then the sum of the numbers is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of numbers = 2 : 3

**LCM** of ratio parts (2 and 3) = 2 × 3 = 6 units

6 units = 84 ⇒ 1 unit = 14

Sum of numbers = (2 + 3) = 5 units

Sum = 5 × 14 = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of two numbers = 84

Ratio of the numbers = 2 : 3

**Formula Used:**

LCM of numbers ax and bx = (a × b) × x (where a and b are coprime)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0bc3ef8f466dd7dc5987dcd12a45c29ee84ea48a2b0b2e354da6fcedcdfecde9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 2x and 3x.

⇒ LCM of 2x and 3x = 6x

⇒ 6x = 84

⇒ x = 84 ÷ 6 = 14

⇒ Sum of the numbers = 2x + 3x = 5x

⇒ Sum = 5 × 14

⇒ Sum = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Relation of LCM and HCF

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF × LCM.

HCF and Ratio Relationship

If two numbers are in the ratio a : b and their HCF is x, then the numbers are ax and bx, and their LCM is a × b × x.

HCF of Coprime Numbers

The HCF of two coprime numbers is always 1, and their LCM is simply the product of the two numbers.</p

questions.question: The surface area of a sphere is 256 π m2. Find its diameter.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Surface Area = 4 π r² = 256 π

⇒ r² = 256 ÷ 4 = 64

⇒ Radius (r) = √64 = 8 m

⇒ Diameter = 2 × 8 = 16 m

**∴ The correct answer is 16m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Surface Area** of the **Sphere** = 256 π m²

**Formula:**

**Surface Area** (S) = 4 π r²

**Diameter** (d) = 2r

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b3abad48d2e885c017bbfd7ef54c711f2d234f89fc48e59a55e92b2a40b46611.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4 × π × r² = 256 × π

⇒ r² = 256 ÷ 4

⇒ r² = 64

⇒ r = √64

⇒ r = 8 m

⇒ Diameter = 2 × r

⇒ Diameter = 2 × 8 = 16 m

**∴ The correct answer is 16m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The amount of space occupied by a **sphere** is calculated using the formula: V = (4/3) × π × r³.

Surface Area of a Hemisphere

For a **hemisphere**, the **Curved Surface Area** (CSA) is 2πr² and the **Total Surface Area** (TSA) is 3πr².

Properties of a Sphere

A **sphere** is a perfectly symmetrical 3D object where all points on the surface are at an equal distance (radius) from the center.</p

questions.question: The equivalent resistance of the series combination of R ohm and 5 ohm is 7 ohm. Here, R is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 ohm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **series combination**, the total resistance is the sum of the individual resistances.
 
• The formula for the **equivalent resistance** in a series combination is: **Rₑq = R₁ + R₂**.
 
• Here, the equivalent resistance is given as **7 ohm**, and one of the resistances is **5 ohm**.
 
• Using the formula: **7 = R + 5**.
 
• Rearranging the equation gives: **R = 7 - 5**, which equals **2 ohm**.
 
• Hence, the missing resistance value **(R)** is **2 ohm**.
 
• This concept is fundamental in understanding **electric circuits** and is used to calculate the total resistance in a series connection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Series Combination**__

 __
 
• In a **series circuit**, the current flowing through each resistor is the same, but the total voltage is divided across the resistors.
 
• The total resistance in a series circuit is always greater than the resistance of any individual resistor.
 
• Series circuits are commonly used in applications like **string lights** and **simple electronic devices**.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Combination**__
 __

questions.question: Amita is 2 years elder than her friend Amrita. Amita's father is twice as old as Amita, and Amrita is twice as old as her sister. The ages of Amita's father and Amrita's sister differ by 43 years. The difference between the ages of Amita and Amrita is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The difference between the ages of **Amita** and **Amrita** is directly mentioned in the question.

The first statement of the question states: "**Amita** is 2 years elder than her friend **Amrita**."

Therefore, the difference between their ages is directly equal to 2 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the age of **Amita** = A

Let the age of **Amrita** = B

Let the age of Amita's **father** = F

Let the age of Amrita's **sister** = S

**Formula/Equations:**

Formulating linear equations from the given statements:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e0c9eb2520b7ab260486b88b7deddfb8629cd6815d9992befa8318f63e20586.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A − B = 2 ⇒ A = B + 2 ----(Equation 1)

⇒ F = 2 × A ----(Equation 2)

⇒ B = 2 × S ⇒ S = B ÷ 2 ----(Equation 3)

⇒ F − S = 43 ----(Equation 4)

Substitute the values of F and S from Equation 2 and Equation 3 into Equation 4:

⇒ 2 × A − B ÷ 2 = 43

Substitute the value of A from Equation 1 into the equation:

⇒ 2 × (B + 2) − B ÷ 2 = 43

⇒ 2 × B + 4 − 0.5 × B = 43

⇒ 1.5 × B + 4 = 43

⇒ 1.5 × B = 39

⇒ B = 39 ÷ 1.5 = 26 years

⇒ A = B + 2 = 26 + 2 = 28 years

Thus, the difference between the ages of Amita and Amrita is:

⇒ A − B = 28 − 26 = 2 years

**∴ The correct answer is 2 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Linear Equation in Two Variables

Solving problems on ages generally requires setting up linear equations representing relations between individuals' ages.

Invariance of Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains constant throughout their lives, regardless of how many years pass.

Ratio and Proportion in Ages

If the ratio of ages of two persons is x : y, and after n years the ratio becomes a : b, we can solve for their present ages using: (x × k + n) ÷ (y × k + n) = a ÷ b.</p

questions.question: If the mean of a data is 65 and its mode is 23, then the median using empirical formula is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **empirical relation** is: 3 × **Median** = **Mode** + 2 × **Mean**

Given **Mean** = 65 and **Mode** = 23

3 × Median = 23 + 2 × 65 = 23 + 130 = 153

Median = 153 ÷ 3 = 51

**∴ The correct answer is 51.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mean** = 65

**Mode** = 23

For a moderately skewed frequency distribution, the **empirical formula** is:

**Calculations:**

⇒ 23 = 3 × Median − 2 × 65

⇒ 23 = 3 × Median − 130

⇒ 3 × Median = 23 + 130

⇒ 3 × Median = 153

⇒ Median = 153 ÷ 3

⇒ Median = 51

**∴ The correct answer is 51.**

**__Additional Information__**

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, the **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are identical (Mean = Median = Mode).

Positively Skewed Distribution

If the data is skewed to the right, the values follow the order: **Mean** > **Median** > **Mode**.

Negatively Skewed Distribution

If the data is skewed to the left, the values follow the order: **Mode** > **Median** > **Mean**.

Applicability of Empirical Formula

This formula is an approximation and works best for **moderately skewed** unimodal distributions.</p

Here, the shift is **3**, so the difference = 2 × 3 = **6**.

questions.question: Two people drive towards each other from two places which are 56 km apart. The speed of the first person is 12 km/h and the speed of the other is 14 km/h. After how long will they be 4 km apart if they start driving at the same time?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** when moving towards each other = 12 + 14 = 26 km/h.

Total distance to be reduced = 56 − 4 = 52 km.

**Time required** = Distance covered ÷ Relative Speed = 52 ÷ 26 = 2 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance between two places = 56 km

Speed of the **first person** (S₁) = 12 km/h

Speed of the **second person** (S₂) = 14 km/h

Required **gap** between them = 4 km

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite direction) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9278691bebf12e1bf13211f62e44cdbe06f453e67caa3bf2c19f0206ab339588.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total initial distance = 56 km

⇒ Target distance apart = 4 km

⇒ Effective distance covered by both = 56 − 4 = 52 km

⇒ **Relative Speed** = 12 + 14 = 26 km/h

⇒ Time taken = 52 ÷ 26 = 2 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move toward each other or away from each other, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the **difference** between their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Time of Meeting

The time taken to meet is calculated as **Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed**, provided they start at the same time.</p

questions.question: Why do covalently bonded compounds have low boiling point?

options.text: Have strong covalent bond within molecules but weak intermolecular force
Have weak covalent bond within molecules but weak intermolecular force
Have strong covalent bond within molecules and also strong intermolecular force
Have strong intermolecular force within molecules but weak covalent bond

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Have strong covalent bond within molecules but weak intermolecular force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Covalently bonded compounds have strong covalent bonds within the molecules, which keep the atoms together in a molecule.
 
• Despite strong intramolecular forces, these compounds exhibit weak intermolecular forces between different molecules.
 
• The weak intermolecular forces (like van der Waals forces) require less energy to break, leading to a lower boiling point.
 
• These compounds usually exist in the form of gases or liquids at room temperature due to their low boiling points.
 
• Examples of covalently bonded compounds with low boiling points include molecular hydrogen (H₂), nitrogen (N₂), and methane (CH₄).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Intermolecular Forces**

 
 
• These are forces of attraction or repulsion which act between neighboring particles (atoms, molecules, or ions).
 
• Types of intermolecular forces include dipole-dipole interactions, London dispersion forces, and hydrogen bonding.
 
 
 
• **Boiling Point**
 
 
• The boiling point of a substance is the temperature at which its vapor pressure equals the external pressure surrounding the liquid.
 
• Strong intermolecular forces result in a higher boiling point as more energy is required to separate the molecules.
 
 
 
• **Polar and Non-Polar Covalent Bonds**
 
 
• Polar covalent bonds occur when electrons are shared unequally between atoms, leading to a distribution of charge.
 
• Non-polar covalent bonds occur when electrons are shared equally, resulting in no overall charge distribution.

**∴ The correct answer is 32 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Thickness** of the block = 5 cm

Volume of a cuboid = Length × Width × Thickness

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1ac1dc0864b658c24d71c3fff9854e3750722965a140658f903871660a50630.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Length** = 4,480 ÷ 140

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper pretends to sell his goods at cost price. However, he uses a false weight on which 200 gm is written, but which actually weighs lesser. Using this false weight, the shopkeeper makes a gain of 25%. The actual measure of the weight used is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

A **gain** of 25% means the ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Selling Price (SP)** is 100 : 125 = 4 : 5.

In **false weight** problems, the ratio of **Actual Weight** to **Marked Weight** is the same as the CP to SP ratio when sold at cost price.

Ratio of weights = 4 : 5 → (Actual Weight) : (200 gm) = 4 : 5.

5 units = 200 gm ⇒ 1 unit = 40 gm.

Actual Weight (4 units) = 4 × 40 gm = 160 gm.

**∴ The correct answer is 160 gm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Weight (True Value) = 200 gm

Percentage Gain = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Gain % = [(True Weight − Actual Weight) ÷ Actual Weight] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ebeacb65810806fafbcebe243421da616aa6e9e63c6b00c473de581e29919b90.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Actual Weight** used by the shopkeeper be 'x' gm.

⇒ 25 = [(200 − x) ÷ x] × 100

⇒ 25 ÷ 100 = (200 − x) ÷ x

⇒ 1 ÷ 4 = (200 − x) ÷ x

⇒ x = 4 × (200 − x)

⇒ x = 800 − 4x

⇒ 5x = 800

⇒ x = 800 ÷ 5

⇒ x = 160 gm

**∴ The correct answer is 160 gm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Shopkeeper Concept

When a shopkeeper sells goods at cost price but uses a **false weight**, the profit is calculated on the **actual weight** delivered, not the marked weight.

Combined Profit Formula

If a shopkeeper marks up the price by k% and also uses a false weight, Total Profit % = [((100+k) × True Weight) ÷ Actual Weight] − 100.

Multiplier Method

The effective multiplier for profit is (True Weight ÷ Actual Weight). If Actual Weight is 160g for 200g, multiplier = 200/160 = 1.25, which represents a 25% gain.</p

questions.question: A sum of money lent on simple interest becomes (7)/(5) of itself in 4 years. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Principal (P)** be 5 units (denominator of the fraction).

The **Amount (A)** becomes 7 units (numerator of the fraction).

**Simple Interest (SI)** = Amount − Principal = 7 − 5 = 2 units.

**Rate (R)** = (Interest ÷ Principal) × (100 ÷ Time).

Rate = (2 ÷ 5) × (100 ÷ 4) = 0.4 × 25 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount (A) = 7/5 of Principal (P)

Time period (T) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0163fedb9544edf29d1eff4c42083932868027ca2e2b7547187d2410a17224f4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = A − P

⇒ SI = (7/5)P − P = (2/5)P

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ (2/5)P = (P × R × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 2/5 = 4R ÷ 100

⇒ 2/5 = R ÷ 25

⇒ R = (2 × 25) ÷ 5

⇒ R = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between Amount and Rate

The amount in simple interest can be directly calculated using the formula A = P(1 + RT/100), where R is the **annual rate** and T is the **time in years**.

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective rate for the entire duration is (R × T)%. In this case, 10% × 4 = 40%, which matches the interest being 2/5 (or 40%) of the principal.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In **Simple Interest**, the interest remains constant every year as it is always calculated on the original **Principal**, unlike Compound Interest where interest is earned on interest.</p

• The focal length (**f**) of a spherical mirror is related to its radius of curvature (**R**) by the formula: **f = R/2.**
 
• In the given question, the focal length of the convex mirror is **1m.**
 
• Using the formula **f = R/2**, we can calculate the radius of curvature as: **R = 2f = 2 × 1 = 2m.**
 
• Thus, the distance between the **centre of curvature** and the **pole** of the convex mirror is **2m.**
